name: ok-recipe
title: Weeknight lentil soup
text:
Weeknight lentil soup

Serves 4. Ready in 40 minutes.

Ingredients

- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 onion, diced
- 2 carrots, diced
- 2 cloves garlic
- 1 teaspoon cumin
- 5 cups vegetable stock
- Juice of half a lemon

Method

Soften the onion and carrots in olive oil for eight minutes. Add the garlic and cumin and stir for one minute. Add the lentils and stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes until the lentils collapse. Blend half the soup, stir it back in and finish with lemon juice and salt.

name: ok-poem
title: Morning Ferry
text:
Morning Ferry

The harbour wakes in shades of tin,
gulls stitch the fog with thread,
and every bench along the rail
holds someone half in bed.

The engine hums a patient note,
the far shore takes its time,
and coffee steam and diesel smoke
agree to share the climb.

name: ok-docs-page
title: Retries and backoff
text:
Retries and backoff

Every client call is retried up to three times on transient failures: connection resets, timeouts and HTTP 429 or 503 responses.

Backoff

The delay doubles after each attempt, starting at 200 ms, with full jitter. Set `maxAttempts` to 1 to disable retries.

Idempotency

Only idempotent requests are retried automatically. For POST requests, pass an idempotency key to opt in.

name: ok-article-about-cookies
title: How cookie consent banners actually work
text:
How cookie consent banners actually work

Most visitors click "Accept all" without reading. But behind the banner sits a consent management platform that records your choice and passes it to advertising partners in a standard string.

When you click "Reject all", the site should stop loading non-essential cookies. Audits regularly find sites that load trackers before any choice is made.

Regulators have started to fine sites whose "Reject" button is harder to find than "Accept". The practical advice: look for a "Manage options" link and check that the choices persist on your next visit.

name: ok-article-about-login
title: What we learned rolling out passkeys
text:
What we learned rolling out passkeys

Six months ago we added passkeys next to the password sign-in form. Today 41% of sign-ins use them.

The biggest surprise was account recovery. Users who lost a device needed a path back in that did not reintroduce passwords, so we added recovery codes at enrolment.

The login page itself changed little: one extra button, "Sign in with a passkey". Support tickets about forgotten passwords dropped by a third.

name: ok-paywall-explainer
title: Are metered paywalls still working?
text:
Are metered paywalls still working?

A metered paywall lets readers see a few free articles a month before the "Subscribe to keep reading" prompt appears. Publishers adopted the model widely in the 2010s.

New data from a group of regional publishers suggests the meter is losing ground to hard paywalls on premium sections combined with free general news. Conversion rates on the hard sections were roughly double.

The trade-off is reach: free articles drive search traffic, which feeds the subscription funnel.

name: ok-error-postmortem
title: Incident: elevated 500 errors on the API
text:
Incident: elevated 500 errors on the API

Between 14:02 and 14:37 UTC, about 8% of API requests returned 500 Internal Server Error.

Cause: a configuration change reduced the database connection pool from 50 to 5 on one region's API servers.

Resolution: we reverted the change and added a check that blocks pool sizes below 20 in production configuration.

No data was lost.

On shipping

A rule I keep relearning: the version you ship this week beats the perfect version you ship next quarter, because only the shipped one tells you what to fix.
